title: L1: incorporate co-change edges into component clustering
description:
Hidden coupling (files that co-change >=50% of shared commits but have no static import edge) reveals architectural relationships invisible to the dependency graph. When clustering for component discovery, these co-change edges should be weighted alongside static edges — they're evidence of behavioral coupling the import graph misses.

Concrete proposal: when building the graph for Louvain/Leiden clustering, add weighted edges for co-change pairs that exceed a correlation threshold (repowise uses 0.5). Weight them below static edges (they're noisier) but above nothing. This should improve component boundary detection for code that's architecturally coupled through shared protocols, parallel config, or implicit contracts rather than explicit imports.

Also surface in orient: "these files are coupled but not by imports" and in review: "your change touched A; B is behaviorally coupled and may need changes too."

Reference: repowise's hidden_coupling biomarker — `repowise/packages/core/src/repowise/core/analysis/health/biomarkers/hidden_coupling.py`. Their implementation joins co_change_partners_json with the static graph edges and fires when correlation >= 0.5 with no import edge in either direction. They exclude test<->production pairs.

Prior art: D'Ambros et al. on co-change as defect signal; the correlation threshold and test-pair exclusion are the key design choices.

acceptance_criteria.text: commits table (hash PK, committed_at INTEGER, author TEXT) and commit_files table (commit_hash FK, file_id FK) populated during parse pipeline from git history
Jaccard coefficient computed from commit_files for all file pairs exceeding the configured threshold
Hidden co-change edges (above threshold, no static ref edge) are added to the clustering graph in build_weighted_adjacency
Test-production file pairs excluded from co-change edges via path heuristic
New config keys in .sutra/components.toml: cochange_threshold (f64, default 0.5), cochange_weight (f64, blending factor), cochange_window_days (u32, default 90)
Staleness guard updated to account for co-change data freshness
Existing sutra_cochange tool continues to work (no regression)

decisions: Persist co-change data in a commit_files table (not on-demand git log). Shared substrate for L4 metrics later.
Use Jaccard coefficient for correlation, configurable threshold defaulting to 0.5 in .sutra/components.toml
Hidden-only edges: only add co-change edges where NO static reference edge exists between the pair
Reasonable default weight with config knob in components.toml for blending factor
Exclude test-production pairs via path heuristic (test/tests/spec/__tests__)
Git history window matches existing cochange tool (90 days) with config override in components.toml
Orient and review surfacing are separate tasks — this task is clustering infrastructure only

Normalized commits(hash, committed_at, author) table alongside commit_files — avoids repeating metadata per file row, gives L4 time-decay and ownership data. Per-function blame rollup is separate/on-demand.

messages.author: user
messages.text: Schema request from 5e brainstorm (sutra/43): L4 health metrics need a normalized commits table alongside commit_files. Requested schema: commits(hash TEXT PK, committed_at INTEGER, author TEXT). This enables change_entropy (time decay), ownership_risk (author attribution), and code_age_volatility (line age) without a separate git log pass. Please widen migration 0024 before it lands.

messages.author: codex
messages.text:
Codex adversarial review — verdict: needs-attention

[high] Clustering staleness ignores co-change graph content changes (src/components.rs:728-738)
is_clustering_stale compares only total commit_file_count. If the 90-day window rolls forward or replace_commit_files swaps rows with different rows but the same count, staleness returns false and clustering uses stale co-change edges. Recommend persisting a freshness token (digest of rows, max committed_at + count, or computed edge digest) and reclustering when it changes.

[high] Failed or empty git-history refresh leaves old co-change rows active (src/pipeline.rs:552-578)
git_commit_files errors are converted to empty vec via unwrap_or_default, and empty results skip replace_commit_files entirely. Transient git failure or valid empty window leaves previous commit_files rows active, silently driving clustering/orient/review with stale data. Recommend distinguishing successful empty history from git failure; clear tables on successful empty scans; propagate/log error on git failures.
